title: Locale edgecase numeric & date promptbank (CJK + RTL)
content:
Purpose:
This working promptbank collects focused cases for numeric, date/time, and currency formatting and translation behavior in CJK (zh, ja, ko) and RTL (ar, he, fa) contexts. The goal is to catch subtle regressions during model onboarding: wrong separators, incorrect symbol placement, broken ICU/pluralization placeholders, bidi/shape errors, and translation distortions when numbers are involved.

Scope and priorities:
- Primary languages: zh-CN, zh-TW, ja-JP, ko-KR, ar-SA, he-IL, fa-IR
- Secondary: en-GB, en-US, fr-FR for cross-checks
- Focus areas: dates, times, currencies, percentages, phone numbers, measurements, digit widths (full/half), punctuation mirroring, ICU placeholder preservation, translation fidelity with numerics.
- Not covered here: deep semantic translation of paragraphs without numbers (separate evals).

How to use this doc (quick):
1) Use the prompt templates below to generate model outputs across model variants and quantization profiles.
2) Run automatic checks (regex + CLDR-based formatter) and produce a CSV of failures.
3) Send failing samples to human raters for severity labeling and cause taxonomy.
4) Record regression stats in the onboarding dashboard and gate on thresholds in the checklist.

Evaluation goals / success metrics:
- Critical errors (dates parsed to wrong day/month, currency invalid symbol/position, ICU placeholders removed or reordered): target < 0.5% on full regression sample.
- Major formatting mismatches (wrong separator, wrong digit width, mirrored punctuation): target < 1.5%.
- Acceptable translation drift for numeric contexts: mean human score >= 4.0/5 on fidelity/naturalness.
- Note: thresholds are intentionally conservative for Dedicated/Private rollouts.

Sampling plan:
- Smoke: 200 prompts per locale (stratified across categories).
- Regression: 2,000 prompts per locale, sampled with heavier weight on edgecases (ambiguous dates, mixed scripts, ICU strings).
- Rater pool: bilingual raters for each locale pair; use cross-rater checks on 10% overlap.
- Priority locales for first pass: zh-CN, ja-JP, ar-SA.

Prompt categories and example templates:
1) Date disambiguation (MM/DD vs DD/MM vs YYYY-MM-DD)
- Template: "Standardize to long-form date in {locale}: '{input_date}' ->"
  - Example (zh-CN): input_date="3/4/2025" (ambiguous)  expected behaviors: prefer ISO or explicit locale-aware expansion; if locale zh-CN assume 2025年3月4日 unless user context says otherwise.
  - Example (en-GB): input_date="3/4/2025" -> 3 April 2025.
  - Edge: "02/03/04" (two-digit year) -> flag as ambiguous, ask clarification or follow configurable policy (prefer 2004).

2) Timezone + 12/24-hour normalization
- Template: "Convert to {locale} user-readable time: '{input_time}' from UTC to {tz} ->"
  - Example: input_time="2025-05-08T18:30:00Z" locale=ja-JP tz=Asia/Tokyo -> 2025年5月9日 03:30 (24時間) or localized template.
  - RTL nuance: Arabic locales often use Arabic-Indic digits; ensure digits are rendered in correct numeral system when requested.

3) Currency placement and symbol selection
- Template: "Format {amount} in {locale} currency display. Use locale conventions."
  - Example: amount=1234.5 locale=fr-FR currency=EUR -> 1234,50 EUR? (should be 1234,50 €) -- ensure correct symbol, spacing, NBSP if CLDR prescribes.
  - Example (ar-SA): amount=1000 currency=SAR expected: ر.س1,000 or Arabic-Indic digits depending on user preference.
  - Edge: negative currency formatting (() vs -) and accounting formats must match locale rules.

4) Thousand/decimal separators and digit groupings
- Template: "Normalize number: '{input_number}' for locale {locale} ->"
  - Example: input_number="1234567.89" locale=de-DE -> 1.234.567,89
  - CJK: prefer no thousands separator for compact displays in some contexts; document expected behavior per platform config.

5) Full-width vs half-width numerals and punctuation (CJK)
- Template: "Render the following receipt line in {locale}: '{line}' ->"
  - Example: line="Qty: 3 Price: $12.00" locale=ja-JP -> Expected: "数量：３ 価格：￥１２．００" OR half-width depending on policy.
  - We need explicit per-project policy: default to half-width for code-like outputs, full-width for typography-sensitive copy.

6) Bidirectional text and punctuation mirroring (RTL)
- Template: "Embed English alphanumeric in Arabic sentence and normalize bidi: '{sentence_with_ENG_numbers}' ->"
  - Example: "التحديث v2.3 سيصدر في 12/11/2025." Expected: correct visual order, digits maybe Arabic-Indic, punctuation should mirror when necessary.
  - Add tests that introduce LTR runs at beginning/end to trigger DIR heuristics.

7) ICU MessageFormat and placeholder preservation
- Template: "Translate while preserving ICU placeholders: 'You have {count, plural, one{# message} other{# messages}}' -> {target_lang}"
  - Critical: placeholders must remain valid; plural clauses must be correct for target language.
  - Example: English->Arabic: verify plural categories (zero/one/two/few/many/other) and ensure translator output includes those clauses rather than a single numeric substitution.

8) Phone numbers and metadata (country codes, local formats)
- Template: "Format phone '{raw}' for {locale} display ->"
  - Example: raw="+1 (415) 555-2671" locale=zh-CN -> +1 415 555 2671 OR (415) 555-2671 depending on policy.

9) Measurement units and conversion hints
- Template: "Localize units: 'The wall is 8 feet tall' for {locale} ->"
  - Example: locale=ja-JP -> メートル換算提供: "壁の高さは約2.44メートルです。" Provide both original + converted when requested.

10) Mixed-script translations (numbers embedded in text to be preserved)
- Template: "Translate preserving numbers: '{sentence}' ->"
  - Example: "Order 12: deliverables due 2025-03-04." Ensure '12' and date tokens preserved/normalized appropriately for target locale.

Automatic checks (developer-run):
- Run CLDR/ICU-based formatters (via python-babel/ICU) to compare model output against canonical formatting.
- Regex checks for common failures: missing currency symbol, wrong separator, misplaced sign, missing placeholder braces, changed ICU token names.
- Unicode checks: presence of RLM/LRM or explicit bidi control chars; presence of Arabic-Indic numerals (\u0660-\u0669) vs European digits; full-width digits U+FF10-U+FF19.
- Structural check: parseable date with dateutil when format expected; if ambiguous, mark as ambiguous instead of silently converting.

Human rater rubric (brief):
- Score 1-5 for: Fidelity (accurate numeric values preserved), Locale Naturalness (follows conventions), Safety (no masked/misleading values), ICU/Placeholder Integrity (preserved).
- Severity tags: critical, major, minor. Critical = wrong numeric value or removed placeholder; Major = wrong symbol/placement or digit width error that changes readability; Minor = spacing/NBSP or style differences.
- For plural ICU tests: rater must mark whether plural categories are complete and linguistically correct.

Regression detection and gating:
- Compute per-locale rates for each error class. Use baseline model A (current onboarded) and candidate B (new). Flag regression if increase in critical error rate > 0.2% absolute AND statistically significant (p < 0.05) on N regression samples.
- For major errors, regression threshold = 1.0% absolute increase.
- When a regression is flagged: save failing examples, annotate cause (tokenization, formatting rule mismatch, numerals conversion bug, locale map missing), open JIRA ticket with template (include sample id, model config, seed, input, output, expected, automatic check results).

Launch checklist (for model onboarding):
- [ ] Run full regression sample across prioritized locales.
- [ ] Auto-check pass rate above thresholds.
- [ ] Human raters sign off on sample (>=4.0 mean).
- [ ] No open critical JIRA bugs.
- [ ] Document any locale-specific policy deviations in release notes.

Quick examples (copy-paste to run):
1) Date ambiguous: "3/4/25" -> locale=he-IL -> expected: 4 במרץ 2025 OR policy-led answer.
2) ICU plural: "You have {count, plural, one{# file} other{# files}}" -> ar-SA -> must include Arabic plural categories.
3) Full-width: "Invoice total: $2450.00" -> ja-JP -> "請求合計：￥２,４５０．００" OR document-specific choice.
4) Bidi: "Update v2.3 released on 12/11/2025." -> ar-SA -> visually correct ordering with appropriate numerals.

Open questions / TODO (notes to self):
- Decide default numeral system per locale vs per-user-preference (e.g., Arabic-Indic vs European digits). Add config flags in onboarding schema.
- Policy: When to prefer ISO dates vs localized expansion for ambiguous inputs. Need product decision (ticket JIRA-APML-1488).
- Add automated comparison to CLDR "currencySpacing" rules for fine-grained NBSP checks.

References and links:
- CLDR repo and locale examples (internal mirror) - CONFLUENCE-4492
- JIRA epic for onboarding regression infra - JIRA-APML-1423
- Bidi/Unicode notes: https://unicode.org/reports/tr9/
- GitHub PR with sample harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboarding/pull/211

Notes: this is an iterative working list — expect many additions as raters and infra surface new failure modes. Keep this file as the canonical promptbank for numeric/date/currency edgecases in CJK+RTL onboarding passes.

Last updated by Maya (notes): added stricter gating numbers 2026-02-28.
